To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amino acid requirements of the chick can be calculated by a computer model and that the model-calculated requirements are valid for 2-10 weeks of age.

a model, developed on the basis of the amino acid requirements of the chick, can predict the requirements for all amino acids, including the non-essential ones, and can thus be used to calculate a diet which will support optimal growth and feed efficiency.
the amino acid requirements of growing chicks are lower than those recommended by NRC (1977), and that these lower requirements can be calculated with the Hurwitz et al. (1978) model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a computer-based model which can be utilized in the formulation of low-cost, nutritionally balanced, diets for chicks.
the development of a model for the amino acid requirements of the growing chick, and with the use of this model in the design of practical diets.
the development of a computer-based model for the amino acid requirements of growing chicks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model-calculated amino acid requirements of growing broilers are valid.
, for chicks, the model-based diets provide the same growth as NRC (1977) based diets, but with less protein, and, when energy and lipid concentrations are equalized, with the same feed efficiency.
the amino acid requirements calculated on the basis of the model are valid for 2-10-week-old chicks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amino acid requirements of young chicks can be predicted with reasonable precision by the model, and that the protein and amino acid requirements of the young chick can be reduced considerably by the use of the model.
the amino acid requirements of young chicks can be calculated with sufficient accuracy for the design of practical diets.
, in the present experiments, model-calculated amino acid requirements for 2- and 10-week-old broiler chicks, as well as the amino acid profile for the protein of egg white, are valid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model-based diets provided a more economical alternative for the production of broilers.
the model-based amino acid requirements of the chick can be used as a basis for formulating diets for the growing chick.
, with the proper modifications, the model can be applied to the calculation of dietary amino acid requirements for broilers of different ages.
